run: catchfuel-transfer-test (catch-fuel value half / cwo.1 transfer test)
premise: Haiku PANEL caught 2 compiling subtle schema bugs (rfd-codex-schema, rfd-nested-schema) 3/3. Does a catch-derived check help a CHEAPER tier (single terse 'fast skim' Haiku) catch what it misses unaided?
finding: The cheap single-reviewer tier already caught both schema bugs 6/6 WITHOUT the check — the bugs are NOT a cheap-tier blindspot, so catch-derived checks add no demonstrable catch-rate value. Empirically confirms the council's Goodhart lens ('most catches encode failure-modes the membrane already catches reliably'). Catch-fuel is precision-safe (separate probe) but value-null on available data: it would seed already-handled cases. Catch-fuel becomes worthwhile only when a catch is a genuine blindspot for the deployed tier — none appeared. Same root as the escape floor: a competent membrane (even cheap) catches the subtle bugs.
